candidate.answerReason: The four possible powers 1, i, −1, and −i give sums 2, 0, −2, and 0 with their reciprocals.

methods.label: Pair each power with its reciprocal
methods.explanation:
Since \(i^2=-1\), we have \(i^4=1\). Therefore every integer power \(i^n\) is one of
\[
1,\quad i,\quad -1,\quad -i.
\]
This includes negative integers: \(i\ne0\), so powers can also be followed backward using reciprocals. Now \(i^{-n}=1/i^n\), and the reciprocals of the four listed values are respectively
\[
1,\quad -i,\quad -1,\quad i.
\]
Their sums are consequently \(2,0,-2,0\). These exhaust all integers \(n\), and all three distinct sums occur: \(n=0,1,2\) give \(2,0,-2\), respectively. Thus there are exactly \(3\) possible values, choice C.
methods.levelReason: Only the four-step cycle of powers of i, negative integer exponents, and elementary complex addition are needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is evaluating integer powers of i. Complex multiplication establishes the cycle, and negative-exponent meaning supplies reciprocals. Complex addition is recorded in the method because the resulting pairs must be summed. No polar form or general roots-of-unity theory is used.
